texts.facts: This appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 29 of Protection of women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (in short 'PWDV Act') challenging the order dated 26.12.2023 passed on IA No.2 by the learned MMTC-VI, Bengaluru in Crl.Misc.No.50/2023 and directed to pay maintenance of Rs.10,000/- to the petitioners No.1 and 3 from the date of petition till the disposal of the petition. 3. The respondent is appellant in this appeal. The petitioners No.1 and 3 are the respondent No.1 and parties are referred to their ranks as ranks in this appeal for the sake of convenience. The appellant married the respondent No.1 on 27.05.1999 and their marriage is love marriage. Out of the marriage, the respondents No.2 and 3 are born. The appellant is employed in National Scheduled Caste Financial Developmental Corporation, and it is a Central Government Undertaking / PSU. The appellant presently working as Assistant General Manager at Bengaluru Unit. He would retire in the month of February 2027. He purchased the shared house by obtaining the loan from the bank. The outstanding loan is amounting to Rs.37 lakhs, he has to pay monthly EMI of Rs.50,000/-. His mother is aged 92 years and he has to look after her. She is retired Government teacher. The appellant is taking care of the respondents and Crl.A.No.29/2024 providing all facilities to them. When he expressed his willingness to sell the flat shared house, then the respondent No.1 started to object for the same. The respondent No.1 insisted for transfer of apartment to her name for which the appellant did not agreed. The respondent No.1 started quarrelling with the appellant almost everyday and started non-co-operation at home. She stopped cooking food for family members and started harassing the aged mother of the appellant. The respondent No.2 also joined the respondent No.1. They have filed this Crl.Misc.No.50/2023 before the MMTC-VI alleging domestic violence. The respondent filed the objection to the main petition and produced the documents. The respondent No.1 moved IA No.2 for maintenance and also filed IA No.I to restrain the appellant from alienating the apartment. The learned Magistrate granted exparte order dated 19.04.2023 which came to be challenged by the appellant by preferring appeal in Crl. Appeal No.732/2023. But Vijaykumar R Salkute vs Mrunal V Salkute on 17 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83528603/ 2 the same came to be dismissed for the reasons that the order being exparte, the appellant can approach the Magistrate for disposal of IA No.I Crl.A.No.29/2024 on merits. IA No.2 filed by the respondent No.1 for interim maintenance partly allowed. Challenging the order the appellant has preferred the appeal. It is not in dispute that the appellant and the respondents are in the same shared household and the appellant is providing each and every items of the provisions including milk, groceries, vegetable, school and college fees of respondents No.2 and 3 including cooking gas. The respondents are not entitled for interim maintenance. In addition to all, the appellant is paying electricity bill and water bill, monthly maintenance of the apartment, traveling bus charges for respondent No.3 to attend the school daily, tour and travel charges, TV cable charges etc. The home-take salary, after deduction of EMI of the appellant is Rs.80,000/- only. Out of this amount, the appellant spending entire amount for taking care of the respondents and his aged mother and to meet other financial expenses. The respondent No.1 has become totally hostile towards the appellant and aged mother. She is not cooking food for them. Even though mediation was held, it was failed due to adamant stand of the respondents. The Crl.A.No.29/2024 respondent No.1 has no intention of matrimonial ties and renounced world of matrimonial relation with the appellant without any justifiable and legal reasons. Consequently, the appellant has been suffering financially and all sorts of inconvenience. The appellant has filed the M.C. No.4658/2023 before the II Addl. Family Judge, Bengaluru seeking for restoration of conjugal rights. In that petition, the respondent No.1 has sought divorce. The appellant is suffering cruelty in the hands of the respondents No.1 and 2. The respondent No.1 is in the habit of going out of the house during evening times and attend late night parties till midnight and come home in the midnight, as if the appellant is nobody to question her and her outside program and activities. At the instigation of sister of the respondent No.1 who is residing in Singapore, the respondent No.1 cut the relationship with the appellant. On account of these the appellant suffering mental torture and loneliness. The respondents No.1 and 2 are seeing the appellant as if he is their enemy at home, though the appellant and the respondents are living in the shared household. It would Crl.A.No.29/2024 contend that the learned Magistrate has presumed that selling or alienating the apartment without permission of the family members is a kind of domestic violence. This imagination of the learned Magistrate is totally arbitrary and capricious and not acceptable under law. 5. In this case, there is no material whatsoever in support of the domestic violence by the appellant. The learned Magistrate presumed that only evidence provided by the respondent No.1 as sufficient. The respondent No.1 except production of the photo of broken latch not produced any other materials to demonstrate that the appellant has given ill treatment. The respondent No.1 falsely cooked up this latch broking story. It was broken by the respondent No.1 herself. In the absence of any evidence of domestic violence the learned Magistrate erroneously passed an order to pay maintenance amount. Hence, on these among other grounds, the appellant prays to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order passed by the learned Magistrate on IA No.2. Crl.A.No.29/2024 6. The respondents entered appearance by engaging their counsel. The present respondent No.1 has filed petition u/s.12 of PWDV Act against the present appellant before the learned MMTC-VI, Bengaluru seeking protection Crl.A.No.29/2024 order u/S.18 of PWDV Act, residence order u/S.19 of PWDV Act, Monetary relief u/S.20 of PWDV Act, compensation / damages u/S.22 of PWDV Act and also prayed for relief u/S.21 of PWDV Act. The learned Magistrate by allowing interlocutory application filed by the respondent No.1 passed protection order, maintenance order and also passed order restraining the present appellant for alienating the shared household. Since the appellant has filed separate appeal challenging the order passed on IA No. 1 and 3 with regarding restraining him from selling the property. I would not discuss about the same in this appeal and the same is discussed in Crl. Appeal No.1570/2024. 11.
texts.arguments: The definition of domestic violence is defined u/S.3 of PWDV Act which reads Crl.A.No.29/2024 as follows. "3. Definition of domestic violence.--For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence in case it-- Vijaykumar R Salkute vs Mrunal V Salkute on 17 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83528603/ 4 (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes causing physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic abuse; or (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any other person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other property or valuable security; or (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any person related to her by any conduct mentioned in clause (a) or clause (b); or (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or mental, to the aggrieved person. Explanation I.--For the purposes of this section,-- (i) "physical abuse" means any act or conduct which is of such a nature as to cause bodily pain, harm, or danger to life, limb, or health or impair the health or development of the aggrieved person and includes assault, criminal intimidation and criminal force; (ii) "sexual abuse" includes any conduct of a sexual nature that abuses, humiliates, degrades or otherwise violates the dignity of woman; (iii) "verbal and emotional abuse" includes-- (a) insults, ridicule, humiliation, name calling and insults or ridicule specially with regard to not having a child or a male child; and (b) repeated threats to cause physical pain to any Crl.A.No.29/2024 person in whom the aggrieved person is interested; (iv) "economic abuse" includes-- (a) deprivation of all or any economic or financial resources to which the aggrieved person is entitled under any law or custom whether payable under an order of a court or otherwise or which the aggrieved person requires out of necessity including, but not limited to, house hold necessities for the aggrieved person and her children, if any, stridhan, property, jointly or separately owned by the aggrieved person, payment of rental related to the shared house hold and maintenance; (b) disposal of household effects, any alienation of assets whether movable or immovable, valuables, shares, securities, bonds and the like or other property in which the aggrieved person has an interest or is entitled to use by virtue of the Vijaykumar R Salkute vs Mrunal V Salkute on 17 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83528603/ 5 domestic relationship or which may be reasonably required by the aggrieved person or her children or her stridhan or any other property jointly or separately held by the aggrieved person; and (c) prohibition or restriction to continued access to resources or facilities which the aggrieved person is entitled to use or enjoy by virtue of the domestic relationship including access to the shared household. 12.
